clue.text: Be ingratiating to speak in local rising

indicators.note: the speaking word is placed inside the overturned pub, so in signals containment
in a down clue rising means the word for local is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a local is a British pub, the neighbourhood drinking place
to speak is to utter

explanation.surface: Someone sweet-talking a local audience in the regional dialect of a rising town.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'local' is one's neighbourhood pub; in a down light 'rising' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is an idiom for flattering them, being ingratiating.

clue.text: Page included in shrinking material for paper

indicators.note: the page letter sits inside the word for shrinking, so included in signals containment

parts.note: shrinking, as in bashful, means coy

explanation.surface: A newspaper page tucked into a stack of material that is shrinking as it is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Copy is journalists' term for the written text supplied for printing in a newspaper.

clue.text: Rich soup in unfinished pottery

explanation.surface: A thick soup served in a rough, unglazed bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: a creamy shellfish soup and unglazed fired ceramic, also called biscuit.

clue.text: More down-to-earth pro harbouring strange likes

indicators.note: harbouring means holding within, so the word for pro wraps the jumbled letters

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for

indicators.note: strange marks the letters of likes as oddly arranged

explanation.surface: A professional with unusual tastes turns out to be more homespun than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Folksy describes homely, unpretentious manners, so the comparative means more down-to-earth.

clue.text: Crazy family that could lead to one's downfall

definitions.text: that could lead to one's downfall

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
kin means family

explanation.surface: A wild relative whose antics might bring one down.
explanation.definitionFit: A discarded fruit peel is the classic slapstick cause of a slip and fall, and figuratively a blunder that ruins someone.

clue.text: Antelope upset a couple of its young

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the pair is read from the bottom
a couple of means the word for its young appears twice

parts.note: a kid is the young of a goat or antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope distressed about a pair of its offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of' gives KIDKID and 'upset' turns it round, which happens to read the same pairs as KIDKID backwards: DIKDIK.
explanation.definitionFit: A dik-dik is a small African antelope.

clue.text: Aircraft in which I travel around in a whirlwind tour

indicators.note: in places the turned-round travelling phrase inside the jumbled tour
a whirlwind spins things around, so these letters are tossed into a new order
around means turned about, so the phrase I travel is read backwards

parts.note: to travel is to go

explanation.surface: A traveller on a whirlwind tour boarding some kind of aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whirlwind' looks like part of the tour's description but signals the anagram (UTRO), and 'around' reverses the travelling phrase (OGI).
explanation.definitionFit: An autogiro is an early rotorcraft whose unpowered rotor provides lift, a kind of flying machine.

clue.text: State of some Indians in interior is sad

indicators.note: in shows the letters lie inside the phrase interior is sad

explanation.surface: A melancholy mood in the heartland of an Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: Orissa, now spelt Odisha, is a state on India's east coast, home to some of its people.

clue.text: Took a pistol, bagging these animals

indicators.note: bagging means holding within, so the letters are concealed in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A hunter grabbed a gun to bag some animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Okapis are giraffe-related forest mammals of central Africa, an example of animals.

clue.text: Defer or continue support

definitions.meaning: to postpone, as a court ... an execution
a prop or brace, as a corset's or a mast's rope

explanation.surface: Choices about postponing or carrying on with backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Three dictionary senses: postpone legally, remain, and a supporting rope or brace.

clue.text: Hazard on coast also seen in boat joining fleet

indicators.note: joining means the fleet word is attached alongside the rest

parts.note: fleet means fast, quick

indicators.note: seen in shows the word for also is placed within the boat letters

parts.note: SS is steamship, a standard abbreviation for a boat
and means also

explanation.surface: A coastal danger spotted where a boat joins up with a fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' looks like a group of ships beside 'boat' but is the adjective quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksands are wet sands that swallow walkers, a hazard on certain shores.

clue.text: Nonsense about pound — this could bring better profit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the nonsense word goes around the pound letter

parts.note: tripe is nonsense
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing talk about money as rubbish while chasing a bigger return.
explanation.definitionFit: Trebling something triples a return, so the word suggests a threefold, better profit.

clue.text: Highly valued around company, showing early promise

indicators.note: around means the valued word encircles the company letters

parts.note: precious means highly valued

explanation.surface: A firm prized for its early promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A precocious child develops abilities unusually early, showing promise ahead of age.

clue.text: Interior of Sark, island confusedly taken for another

indicators.note: confusedly says the remaining letters are mixed up
interior means the inside, so the outer letters of the phrase Sark island are dropped

explanation.surface: A Channel island confused with a different one; Sark is a small Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interior of' strips S and D from SARKISLAND, leaving ARKISLAN, which 'confusedly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The island nation's present name replaced another, Ceylon, so it took one name in place of a former one.

clue.text: Guns for wars? Sounds like the opposite

indicators.note: sounds like signals a word spoken that matches the entry in sound

parts.note: the opposite of wars is peace, so plural peaces

explanation.surface: A wry remark that weapons made for war have a name suggesting their contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces is a term for firearms or artillery, the guns soldiers carry into war.

clue.text: Festival in French city I attend, initially

parts.note: en is French for in
Caen is a French city in Normandy

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of attend

explanation.surface: Someone attending a festival in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' serves both: EN is French for 'in', and CAEN is the French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Encaenia is a commemorative celebration, notably Oxford University's annual ceremony honouring benefactors.

clue.text: Out of order, like 15 in rows and columns here

definitions.text: like 15 in rows and columns here
definitions.meaning: smashed into bits, like the answer to 15, as several grid entries are split up

explanation.surface: A grid in disarray, its lines and columns in fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken means not working and also in fragments, as things in pieces are.

clue.text: Some time to relax in posh chap's neighbourhood

indicators.note: the possessive places the neighbourhood word ahead of the posh chap

parts.note: in the neighbourhood of means nigh, near
a toff is a posh person, British slang for an upper-class man

explanation.surface: Taking a break in a wealthy man's part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in posh chap's neighbourhood' reads as near a toff: NIGH TOFF. A toff is British slang for an upper-class gent.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening free from work is a period of leisure to unwind.

clue.text: Marxist set occupying non-Western quarters

indicators.note: occupying means settling inside, so the set word goes within the quarters

parts.note: compass quarters other than west: E, N, S
to set, as a jelly does, is to gel

explanation.surface: A group of leftists taking over rooms in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote the Communist Manifesto with Marx, a founding Marxist.

clue.text: Insular Spaniard former PM is able to set right

parts.note: John Major was British Prime Minister 1990-97
can means is able

explanation.surface: A former British premier claiming he can put things right.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major was a British Prime Minister in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Majorca, a Spanish Balearic island, is an islander of Spain.

clue.text: In one part of house, install new canopy

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: install means putting something inside, so the new letter goes into the house part

parts.note: a wing is a section of a large house

explanation.surface: Fitting a fresh canopy in one section of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a sheet of canvas stretched over a window or doorway as shelter, a canopy.

clue.text: Gentle and good in part of Africa

indicators.note: the good letter goes inside the country, so in signals containment

parts.note: Benin is a country of West Africa

explanation.surface: Mild-mannered and kind people in a region of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means kindly and mild, a synonym for gentle.

clue.text: Opposite of leading part in Shakespeare comedy

definitions.meaning: the lowest place, as against the top
the weaver who wears an ass's head in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: An actor playing the lead in a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest position is the reverse of top or leading, and Nick Bottom is the comic weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: With net initially twisted, I attach lure

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of net are turned into a new order

parts.note: to cement is to attach firmly

explanation.surface: A fisherman twists a net, then fixes on bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' makes ENT from NET, placed first, which is what 'initially' says.
explanation.definitionFit: An enticement is something that tempts or attracts, a synonym for lure as a noun.

clue.text: Old German understood what Dutch and Irish have in common

parts.note: got means understood, as in I got it

parts.words: what Dutch and Irish have in common
parts.note: both words end in the same letter, H

explanation.surface: Grasping what links two European peoples and their languages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were an ancient Germanic people, so an old German tribe member.

clue.text: Game, or its start, as heard on radio

definitions.meaning: a sport played with clubs and balls

definitions.text: its start, as heard on radio
definitions.meaning: the code word for G, the first letter of game, in the radio phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sports commentator naming the game, or how it begins, over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the sport with clubs and holes, and the NATO alphabet's word for G.

clue.text: Nightmarish males occupying certain cubicles

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the answer lies within the words certain cubicles

explanation.surface: Frightening men lurking in particular booths.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are male demons said to visit sleepers, figures of nightmare.

clue.text: Steal stuff left after work in spell

indicators.note: stuff means pack inside, so the work-and-left letters are crammed into the spell word

parts.note: a shift is a spell of work

indicators.note: after places the left letter behind the work letters

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A thief pockets goods left out after a stint at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal stuff' looks like the definition, but 'stuff' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoplift is to steal goods from a store, a specific kind of theft.
